scripts.initialize:
set -euo pipefail

# gstack, cloned fresh on every build (Michael's setup standard, 2026-11-10). The explicit rm -rf is deliberate: each snapshot build clones gstack again rather than reusing whatever the image carries.
rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/gstack"
git clone --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/garrytan/gstack.git "$HOME/.local/share/gstack"
"$HOME/.local/share/gstack/bin/gstack-capy-install" --require claude,codex,patch

# The site's dependencies, installed the way the build workflow installs them (`.github/workflows/build-check.yml`).
npm ci

# The Python packages `scripts/extract.py --check` imports (lxml, Pillow). `--user` keeps them under `$HOME`, so the system interpreter is untouched.
python3 -m pip install --user --break-system-packages --quiet -r requirements.txt

# The headless browser `npm run verify` drives. CI does not need it; every fidelity check on this repo does.
npx playwright install --only-shell chromium

# The stamp `refresh` compares against, so a restored machine skips this install.
printf '%s\n' "$(sha256sum package.json package-lock.json requirements.txt | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)" > node_modules/.capy-install-stamp
scripts.refresh:
set -euo pipefail

stamp=node_modules/.capy-install-stamp
inputs=$(sha256sum package.json package-lock.json requirements.txt | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
if [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ "$(cat "$stamp" 2>/dev/null || true)" != "$inputs" ]; then
  npm ci
  python3 -m pip install --user --break-system-packages --quiet -r requirements.txt
  npx playwright install --only-shell chromium
  printf '%s\n' "$inputs" > "$stamp"
fi

commands.name: verify
commands.command: BASE=/jennymakunas.com/ npm run build && BASE=/jennymakunas.com/ npm run verify
